test_name: Maternal Screen (Triple Test) Second Trimester Test
page_title: Second Trimester Test Price, Range and Preparation | Metropolis Healthcare
preparation: Completely filled maternal TRF with barcode and latest USG report required. History is mandatory

faqs.question: What is the best time to take the Maternal Screen (Triple Test) Second Trimester Test?
faqs.answer: The test is recommended between 14 and 22.6 weeks of pregnancy, ideally between 15 and 17 weeks for better reliability.

faqs.question: Is overnight fasting mandatory for the Maternal Screen (Triple Test) Second Trimester Test, and for how long?
faqs.answer: Fasting is not required. You can eat and drink normally before the test.

faqs.question: Can dehydration affect my Maternal Screen (Triple Test) Second Trimester Test results?
faqs.answer: Severe dehydration is unlikely to significantly affect results, but maintaining normal hydration is always advisable before any blood test.

faqs.question: How should I prepare my diet and medications before the Maternal Screen (Triple Test) Second Trimester Test?
faqs.answer: No special diet is needed. Inform your doctor about any medical conditions and ensure accurate gestational age details are provided.

faqs.question: How is the blood draw procedure performed for the Maternal Screen (Triple Test) Second Trimester Test?
faqs.answer: A healthcare professional collects about 3 ml of blood from a vein in your arm using standard sterile technique.

faqs.question: Are there any risks to the test?
faqs.answer: Risks are minimal and similar to any routine blood test. You may experience mild pain or slight bruising at the needle site.

faqs.question: What level of Maternal Screen (Triple Test) Second Trimester Test is normal?
faqs.answer: Results are reported as risk ratios and MoM values. A screen negative result indicates low risk, while a screen positive result suggests higher risk and may require further testing.
